units.§1: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Problem. An agent faces an MDP whose reward parameter theta is unknown but fixed within an episode. It maintains a posterior over theta and acts on the belief state (Bayes-adaptive MDP).
units.§2: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Proposition 1. With a parameter fixed per episode, history-dependent policies can exceed history-independent policies; the excess equals the value of the information that past observations carry about theta. Assumptions: finite horizon, observed rewards, a prior shared by all policies.
units.§3: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Computation. Small finite instances are solved exactly by enumerating deterministic history policies; the cost grows doubly exponentially in the horizon.
